name: Existing Project Feature Workflow
description: For work against something already running — EXISTING_PROJECT_FEATURE, BUG_FIX, and TECHNICAL_IMPROVEMENT all use this one template (see WorkType's own docstring in app/models/enums.py for why). Skips Problem Discovery and a full HLD — those only make sense for a brand-new project with nothing to scan yet. Instead: capture the change as a structured intake, scan the existing system for real context, analyze impact, run a focused (not full-product) solution discovery, and produce only the architecture DELTA the change actually causes. Story Crafting is the same shared stage the default template uses (same agentKey/RICH_DEFAULT_PROMPTS entry) — it just receives a different set of approved inputs here. After Story Crafting is approved, this template ends: Jira sync and Story Work Lanes are the SAME per-story mechanisms the default template already hands off to (see app/services/story_delivery.py, app/services/story_jira_sync.py) — not a second, template-specific copy of either.

nodes.name: Feature Intake
nodes.description: Capture the change request itself — what it is, why it's needed, current vs. expected behavior, which existing product/module it touches, and where to find it (repo, Jira project, Confluence). Replaces Requirement Intake for this work type; there is no Problem Discovery stage here.

nodes.name: Existing System Context Scan
nodes.description: Before proposing anything, understand what's actually there today — modules, files/folders, APIs, UI areas, data model, integrations, and current architecture assumptions — grounded in the connected repository where one exists. Never proposes implementation, stories, or code; separates confirmed facts from assumptions.

nodes.name: Impact Analysis
nodes.description: Given the approved intake and system context, identify exactly what this change touches — modules, APIs, screens, database entities, integrations, permissions, performance, testing, deployment/config, backward compatibility, and data migration — and recommend whether an HLD Delta is enough or the change is big enough to warrant a full HLD update.

nodes.name: Mini Solution Discovery
nodes.description: A focused solution direction for this one feature/change only — not a rewrite of the product's overall solution. Functional/non-functional requirements, data and integration requirements, UX considerations, constraints the existing system imposes, assumptions, risks, and open questions. No LLD, no code.

nodes.name: HLD Delta
nodes.description: Only the architecture CHANGE this feature causes — new/changed modules, APIs, data flow, database ownership, security, performance/scalability, observability, deployment/config — plus an Architecture Decision Record and an approval checklist. Does not rewrite the full HLD unless Impact Analysis recommended FULL_HLD_UPDATE. Story Crafting stays locked until this is approved.

nodes.name: Story Crafting
nodes.description: The same Story Crafting stage the default SDLC template uses (identical agentKey/prompt) — here it breaks the approved HLD Delta into implementable stories instead of a full HLD. Once approved, each story runs its own LLD/Implementation Plan/Implementation/PR Review/Testing individually via the Stories tab, exactly like the default template.
